theory.intro: A quartic $ax^{4}+bx^{3}+cx^{2}+dx+e=0$ with roots $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ gives four combinations of the roots, one from each coefficient. Their signs alternate: $-\dfrac{b}{a}$, $\dfrac{c}{a}$, $-\dfrac{d}{a}$, $\dfrac{e}{a}$.
facts: The four combinations alternate in sign: $-\dfrac{b}{a}$, $+\dfrac{c}{a}$, $-\dfrac{d}{a}$, $+\dfrac{e}{a}$.
The product of all four roots is $\alpha\beta\gamma\delta=\dfrac{e}{a}$.
A missing power has coefficient $0$: with no $x^{3}$ term, $b=0$ and the sum of roots is $0$.
steps: Identify coefficients $a, b, c, d, e$ from standard quartic form $ax^{4}+bx^{3}+cx^{2}+dx+e=0$.

foundation.question_text: Find the sum of the roots of $x^{4}-3x^{3}+5x^{2}-7x+2=0$.
For the quartic $x^{4}+2x^{3}-6x^{2}+4x-9=0$, find the sum of the products of the roots taken two at a time ($\sum\alpha\beta$).
Find the sum of the products of the roots taken three at a time ($\sum\alpha\beta\gamma$) for $2x^{4}-5x^{3}+3x^{2}+8x-1=0$.
Find the product of all four roots of $3x^{4}+4x^{3}-2x^{2}-5x-12=0$.
Find the sum of the roots of $4x^{4}-8x^{2}+3x-1=0$.
Find the product of the roots of $5x^{4}-10x^{3}+7x^{2}-2=0$.
If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are the roots of $x^{4}-4x^{3}+6x^{2}-5x+2=0$, find $\frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{1}{\gamma}+\frac{1}{\delta}$.

development.question_text: For the quartic $2x^{4}-3x^{3}+4x^{2}-6x+3=0$, evaluate the sum of the reciprocals of pairs of roots: $\sum\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}$.
The quartic equation $x^{4}-4x^{3}-x^{2}+16x-12=0$ has roots $1, 2, 3,$ and $\delta$. Find $\delta$ using the product of roots.
The equation $x^{4}-6x^{3}+11x^{2}-6x=0$ has roots $0, 1, 2,$ and $\delta$. Find $\delta$ using the sum of roots.
Two of the roots of $x^{4}-5x^{3}+5x^{2}+5x-6=0$ are $1$ and $-1$. Find the sum $\gamma+\delta$ and product $\gamma\delta$ of the remaining roots.
For the quartic $3x^{4}-2x^{3}+7x-8=0$, find the sum of all products of three roots ($\sum\alpha\beta\gamma$).
For the quartic $2x^{4}+5x^{3}-3x+1=0$, find the sum of the products of roots taken two at a time ($\sum\alpha\beta$).

If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are the roots of $x^{4}-2x^{3}+3x^{2}-4x+5=0$, evaluate $\frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma}+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta\delta}+\frac{1}{\alpha\gamma\delta}+\frac{1}{\beta\gamma\delta}$.

mastery.question_text: The quartic equation $x^{4}-2x^{3}-7x^{2}+8x+12=0$ has two roots that are opposites ($\alpha$ and $-\alpha$). Find all four roots.
The quartic $x^{4}+px^{3}+qx^{2}+rx+s=0$ has roots $\alpha, -\alpha, \beta, \frac{1}{\beta}$. Show that $s = -\alpha^{2}$ and $q = 1+s$.
Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ be the roots of $2x^{4}-6x^{3}+4x^{2}-5x+1=0$. Evaluate $(\sum\alpha)(\sum\alpha\beta)$.
